content:
Requirement R10 (input): Command Takeover. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to command the takeover of a UAV..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-10.1, F-10.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: 2-3 distinct interaction flows, labeled Be-10.<F>.1, Be-10.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-10.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** After a takeover request is acknowledged (R09 → confirmation), let the pilot issue the actual command that executes the takeover procedure — commanding connection with the UAV and assuming control (UC 4.2.2–4.2.3).

Distinction from R09: R09 *requests permission*; R10 *executes* the granted takeover. This is the commit action that triggers the aircraft-UAV connection sequence.

**Function candidates:**

**F-10.1 — Execute the takeover command (commit to assume control).**
The goal: give the pilot a means to command the takeover procedure once acknowledgment is received. Single teleology — turn a granted request into an active control transfer. Maps directly to 4.2.2–4.2.3.

**F-10.2 — Arm/gate the takeover command against premature or accidental execution.**
The goal: ensure the takeover is only commanded when the pilot deliberately intends it (guard against inadvertent commit in a high-workload cockpit). Distinct goal: not "how to send" but "ensure intentionality of a safety-consequential control transfer." This is a *conditioning* function on the command, not the command itself.

**F-10.3 — Convey takeover-readiness state to the pilot (is the command available/valid now?).**
The goal: make the pilot aware whether commanding takeover is currently permissible (acknowledgment received, link available). Distinct from executing — it's about awareness of command eligibility.

**My steer:** F-10.1 is the core of R10. F-10.3 overlaps heavily with R08 (notification of the acknowledgment) and R09's confirmation delivery — likely already covered, so I'd not open it fresh here. F-10.2 is genuinely distinct and relevant given the safety-critical, occupied-hands context: an accidental takeover has operational consequences.

Recommend closing on **F-10.1** as primary, and deciding whether **F-10.2** (arming/guard) is worth carrying as a second Function or folded into F-10.1's Behaviour as a confirm-step.

Which way do you want to go?

**F-10.1 — Execute the takeover command (commit to assume control).**

Closed.

Moving to Behaviour for F-10.1. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard.

The flow to realize: pilot has received acknowledgment (R09/R08) → pilot commands takeover → HMI transmits (4.2.2–4.2.3) → downstream connection/status confirmations come back via R08.

Note: the guard/intentionality concern from F-10.2 (which we dropped) has to land *somewhere* — so the commit-safety question shows up here as a Behaviour choice.

**Be-10.1.1 — Single deliberate commit (one-shot).**
Pilot invokes takeover command in one action (tap the COMMAND TAKEOVER affordance / press bezel OSS). Immediate transmit. Fastest, lowest workload. Risk: no guard against accidental commit — but takeover only executes if acknowledgment was already received, so the affordance is inert until then (state-gated availability, not an active confirm step).

**Be-10.1.2 — Two-step armed commit (confirm-to-execute).**
Pilot arms the command (first action exposes/enables an EXECUTE affordance), then commits (second action). Guards against inadvertent transfer. Higher deliberateness, one extra action. Absorbs the F-10.2 intentionality concern into the flow.

**Be-10.1.3 — Press-and-hold commit.**
Single sustained action (hold touch target or hold bezel OSS for a dwell) triggers transmit on release/threshold. One gesture, but inherently deliberate — filters accidental brush contacts. Compromise between .1 and .2.

**My steer:** Be-10.1.2. This is a safety-consequential control transfer (assuming command of another operator's UAV), so an explicit confirm-to-execute is justified — and it's where the dropped F-10.2 lives. Be-10.1.1's state-gating helps but doesn't prevent a deliberate-looking accidental tap. Be-10.1.3 is a reasonable lighter alternative if you want to avoid the extra affordance.

Both paths must stay modality-complete (Touch and Keyboard each able to complete the full commit).

Which behaviour?
.1, allowed to press after a confirmation from the takeover request

**Be-10.1.1 — Single deliberate commit (one-shot), state-gated on takeover-request confirmation.**

The COMMAND TAKEOVER affordance is inert/disabled until the R09 request acknowledgment (delivered via R08) is received. Once confirmed, the affordance becomes active and a single action (Touch tap or bezel OSS press) transmits the takeover command (4.2.2–4.2.3). No separate confirm step — the prior acknowledgment *is* the gate.

Modality-complete: Touch tap on WAD affordance OR bezel OSS press, each completes the full commit alone.

Closed.

Moving to Structure for Be-10.1.1.

**S-10.1.1.1 — Dedicated COMMAND TAKEOVER button, surfaced on the takeover confirmation delivery.**
A single WAD touch button (Touch) + mapped bezel OSS (Keyboard), enabled only when the request-acknowledged state is active. Placed on/adjacent to the R08 confirmation pop-up or messages-tab entry that delivered the takeover ack — so the commit lives where the pilot reads the "granted" message.

**S-10.1.1.2 — Reuse the R09 unified takeover control, state-morphed to EXECUTE.**
R09 already gave three shared invocation surfaces (dedicated button, option ring on the UAV, detail panel). Reuse the same takeover control element; once ack is received, its label/state flips from REQUEST to COMMAND TAKEOVER. Same Touch + bezel OSS binding. Single control surface across request→command lifecycle — no new element, minimal cockpit clutter.

**S-10.1.1.3 — UAV-anchored commit via detail panel only.**
Command affordance lives solely in the selected-UAV detail panel (from R09). Pilot opens the UAV's panel, the COMMAND TAKEOVER row is enabled post-ack, commits via Touch or bezel OSS. Ties commit to explicit UAV selection context.

**My steer:** S-10.1.1.2. R09 deliberately built a unified, shared takeover control with three invocation surfaces; the takeover *lifecycle* (request → granted → command) is naturally one control that changes state, not two separate widgets. Morphing REQUEST→COMMAND keeps the pilot's locus of action fixed and reuses all three surfaces, staying consistent with R09's shared-structure decision. 

Flag: this structure is **shared with R09** (same control element, extended with an EXECUTE state) — not exclusive to R10. The enabling-gate logic also depends on R08's confirmation delivery.

S-10.1.1.1 is cleaner if you want the commit co-located with the confirmation message rather than on the UAV control; S-10.1.1.3 is the most context-explicit but drops the fast dedicated-button path.

Which structure?
.1, .3  and maybe on the ring that was planned last Requirement

**S-10.1.1.1 + S-10.1.1.3 + option-ring surface (from R09) — three shared invocation surfaces, state-gated to COMMAND TAKEOVER.**

Consolidated structure:

- **Dedicated COMMAND TAKEOVER button** — WAD touch button + mapped bezel OSS (Keyboard), co-located with the R08 confirmation delivery (pop-up / messages-tab entry). Enabled only once request-ack is received. (S-10.1.1.1)
- **UAV detail panel row** — COMMAND TAKEOVER row in the selected-UAV detail panel, Touch or bezel OSS, enabled post-ack. Context-explicit commit tied to UAV selection. (S-10.1.1.3)
- **Option ring entry** — the R09 press-and-hold option ring on the UAV gains a COMMAND TAKEOVER segment, active only post-ack. Touch select or bezel-stepped select + OSS confirm. (ring surface)

All three enabled by the same state gate (request-acknowledged, via R08); each is modality-complete (Touch and Keyboard both complete the commit alone).

**Flag:** this mirrors R09's three-surface pattern exactly — dedicated button, detail panel, option ring — all **shared with R09**, extended here with the post-ack COMMAND TAKEOVER state. Consolidation later should treat these as one lifecycle control set (REQUEST → COMMAND) across R09/R10, not duplicate widgets. Enabling logic depends on R08.

Structure closed.

**R10 summary:**
- **F-10.1** — Execute the takeover command (commit to assume control).
- **Be-10.1.1** — Single deliberate one-shot commit, state-gated on takeover-request confirmation.
- **S-10.1.1.1 / .3 / ring** — three shared invocation surfaces (dedicated button, UAV detail panel row, option-ring segment), all reused/extended from R09, gated by R08 confirmation, each modality-complete.

R10 ready to close — confirm?

**S-10.1.1.1 — Dedicated COMMAND TAKEOVER button**

- **Where:** co-located with the R08 confirmation delivery — i.e., attached to the pop-up (or the messages-tab entry) that announced "takeover request granted." The commit sits where the pilot reads the ack.
- **Touch path:** single tap on a WAD touch button labeled COMMAND TAKEOVER.
- **Keyboard path:** a bezel OSS mapped to that same button; single press.
- **State gate:** button rendered inert/greyed until R08 delivers the request-acknowledged event; becomes active on ack; reverts after commit (or on timeout/link-loss).
- **Character:** fastest, lowest-workload commit — no navigation, no UAV re-selection. Best for hands-busy immediate action.

**S-10.1.1.3 — UAV detail panel row**

- **Where:** inside the selected-UAV detail panel (the R09 detail-panel surface). A COMMAND TAKEOVER row/line item within that panel.
- **Touch path:** tap the row.
- **Keyboard path:** bezel rotary steps focus to the row + OSS press to activate (or UCP-driven selection).
- **State gate:** row disabled until ack for *that* UAV; enabled post-ack.
- **Character:** context-explicit — commit is bound to an open, identified UAV. Guards against commanding the wrong UAV when several are in play. Slower (requires panel open).

**Option-ring segment**

- **Where:** the R09 press-and-hold radial option ring invoked on a UAV glyph (on Map or UAV list). Adds a COMMAND TAKEOVER segment to that ring.
- **Touch path:** press-and-hold on the UAV → ring opens → slide/tap the COMMAND TAKEOVER segment → release to commit.
- **Keyboard path:** bezel rotary rotates segment selection + OSS confirms.
- **State gate:** the segment appears/enables only post-ack for that UAV; otherwise hidden or greyed.
- **Character:** spatial/in-context — commit directly from the UAV's map or list position without opening a full panel. Middle ground between the fast dedicated button and the explicit detail panel.

**Common to all three:**
- Same underlying takeover-command action; three entry points into it.
- All gated by the same R08 request-acknowledged state.
- Each independently modality-complete (Touch alone or Keyboard alone completes the commit).
- All are R09 surfaces reused and extended with the post-ack COMMAND TAKEOVER state — shared lifecycle control, not new widgets.

One design question worth settling: do you want all three **simultaneously active** post-ack (max redundancy, three ways to commit the same thing), or is one the primary and the others fallback? R09 surfaced all three for the request; mirroring that keeps consistency, but three live commit paths for a safety-consequential action is worth a conscious choice.

Relabeling.

**S-10.1.1.1 — Dedicated COMMAND TAKEOVER button**
Co-located with the R08 confirmation delivery (pop-up / messages-tab). Touch: single tap on WAD button. Keyboard: mapped bezel OSS press. Gated inert until R08 ack; fastest, lowest-workload commit.

**S-10.1.1.2 — Option-ring segment**
R09 press-and-hold radial ring on the UAV glyph (Map / UAV list), extended with a COMMAND TAKEOVER segment. Touch: press-and-hold → ring → select segment → release. Keyboard: bezel rotary selects segment + OSS confirm. Segment enabled only post-ack for that UAV; spatial/in-context commit.

**S-10.1.1.3 — UAV detail panel row**
COMMAND TAKEOVER row inside the selected-UAV detail panel. Touch: tap row. Keyboard: bezel rotary to focus + OSS activate. Row disabled until ack for that UAV; context-explicit, guards against wrong-UAV commit.

All three: same takeover-command action, gated by R08 request-acknowledged state, each modality-complete, all reused/extended from R09 surfaces.

**Updated R10 structure set:** S-10.1.1.1 (dedicated button), S-10.1.1.2 (option ring), S-10.1.1.3 (detail panel row).

Still open: simultaneously active vs. primary+fallback. Confirm to close R10.
